description: Training data for Go syntax error fixing. Each pattern maps an error message substring to a fix operation.

patterns.description: Statement outside function body - usually means a function declaration is missing its opening brace
Function declaration is missing its parameter list parentheses before the opening brace or signature body
examples: func calculatea, b int) int { return a + b }

patterns.description: Code found outside any function - usually a missing opening brace on the previous function
Type declaration (usually a struct) is missing its opening brace, e.g. 'type named struct' followed by a field name without '{'
Type declaration missing its opening brace after 'struct' keyword
Duplicate type in function parameters like 'a, b int int' instead of 'a, b int'
examples: func add(x int, y int int)

patterns.match: unexpected name int in parameter list
patterns.description: Extra type name in parameter list
Missing closing parenthesis in function parameter list like 'func calculate(a, b int'
Unclosed code block - usually caused by a missing closing brace at the end of a function, struct, or conditional block
File ends unexpectedly - usually missing closing braces
Missing opening parenthesis in function call or declaration
Missing 'func' keyword before function name
Package imported but not used in the file
Using a name that hasn't been declared - may need an import
Using a symbol that hasn't been defined - may need an import
Variable declared but never used

patterns.match: missing return at end of function
patterns.description: Function with a return type signature reaches the end of its body without returning a value
Function has more return values than declared in signature
Missing semicolon or automatic semicolon insertion failure, often due to improper statement line-wrapping
Trying to assign to something that can't be assigned to
Type mismatch between expected and actual value
General syntax error where a token appears where it is not valid, often caused by a typo, missing punctuation, or malformed expression
Reference to a variable, function, or type that has not been declared or imported in the current scope

patterns.match: too many arguments in call to
patterns.description: Function call provides more arguments than the function signature defines

patterns.match: not enough arguments in call to
patterns.description: Function call omits required arguments defined in the function signature

patterns.match: cannot use .* (variable of type .*) as type .* in argument to
patterns.description: Type mismatch when passing an argument to a function or assigning a value to a typed variable

patterns.match: no new variables on left side of :=
patterns.description: Short variable declaration used without introducing at least one new variable
Package is imported at the top of the file but never referenced in the code
Local variable is declared with var or := but never referenced in the function body
Number of variables on the left side of an assignment does not match the number of values returned on the right side
Attempting an unsupported operator or operation between incompatible types (e.g., adding a string to an integer)
A type identifier was expected in a declaration or type assertion, but a different token was found
Multiple methods with the exact same receiver and name defined on a type
examples:
func (p *Point) String() string { return "" }
func (p *Point) String() string { return "" }

patterns.description: Variable declared using := or var multiple times within the same scope block
Attempting to write to an unassignable entity, such as a constant, a function result, or a map element value directly
An expression that does not evaluate to a boolean is used inside an if, for, or switch statement condition

patterns.match: invalid operation: shift count .* must be unsigned integer
patterns.description: Bitwise shift operation uses a signed integer or non-integer value for the shift amount
Array, slice, or string indexing operation uses a constant literal index that exceeds bounds or is negative

patterns.match: cannot assign to struct field .* in map
patterns.description: Attempting to modify a field of a struct directly inside a map value because map elements are not addressable
Binary operator used with two operands of different underlying types without explicit conversion
examples:
var a int = 5
var b float64 = 3.2
res := a + b

patterns.description: Using a 'for range' loop on a data type that is not supported (e.g., a basic integer or a boolean)
Slice indices are out of order, negative, or invalid for the target collection type

patterns.match: use of builtin function .* not in function call
patterns.description: Referencing a built-in function name like len or make as a variable value rather than calling it
An operator or keyword was provided where an expression operand (like a literal or variable) was expected
Incorrect syntax when attempting to use a method as a function value via a type selector

patterns.match: mixture of field:value and value elements in struct literal
patterns.description: Combining keyed and unkeyed field initializations inside a single struct literal
Initializing a struct field name that does not exist in the struct definition
Omitting the type name when initializing a composite literal element within another literal
Using a runtime variable or expression instead of a constant integer literal for an array size declaration
Defining the same map key multiple times within a single map literal initialization
Defining a method on an invalid receiver type such as a basic type, pointer, or interface
Type assertion or conversion between types that do not share an interface implementation relationship
Using an unhashable type (like a slice, map, or function) as a key in a map definition
Local variable declaration shadows an outer scope variable or package-level identifier
Attempting to take the memory address of an unaddressable value such as a constant, map item, or literal
Using a break, continue, or goto statement with a label name that has not been declared
Declaring the same loop or block label identifier multiple times within the same function scope

patterns.match: break outside loop, switch, or select
patterns.description: Using a break statement outside of any enclosing loop, switch, or select construct
Using a continue statement outside of a for loop construct
Using a fallthrough statement outside of a switch case block or at the end of a switch statement
Global package scope variables initialized using short variable declaration syntax instead of var
Source file declares a package name that differs from other files in the same directory folder
examples: package main // file is in 'utils' directory

patterns.description: Go source code file does not begin with a valid package clause declaration
Using the blank identifier _ as a normal value expression instead of a write-only target

patterns.match: type .* has no field or method
patterns.description: Calling a method name that does not exist on the given struct type or interface

patterns.match: go statement not at top level
patterns.description: Using the 'go' keyword improperly inside expression contexts rather than before a function call statement
Function returns more values than its declared return type signature allows

patterns.match: expression in defer must be call
patterns.description: Using a defer keyword followed by a non-function call expression

patterns.match: empty rune literal or unclosed rune
patterns.description: Rune literal initialized with empty single quotes or missing a closing single quote character

patterns.match: more than one character in rune literal
patterns.description: Placing multiple characters or a string inside single quotes instead of double quotes
Trying to reference or initialize a private, unexported field from an external package block
Comparing a non-nillable type like an integer or boolean against the nil identifier
examples:
var x int = 5
if x == nil {

patterns.match: invalid operation: map key type .* is comparable; it is not comparable
patterns.description: Using a struct or array containing uncomparable fields (like slices or maps) as a map key

patterns.match: tag is not a string literal
patterns.description: Struct field tag is defined using unquoted text or invalid syntax characters
Generic type instantiation provides an incorrect number of type parameters
Using a generic constraint interface as a regular variable type or function parameter type directly
Embedded fields share overlapping field names, creating ambiguity during selector resolution

patterns.match: init function must have no arguments and no return values
patterns.description: Defining an init function signature with input parameters or return values
Attempting to call the package-level init function explicitly within code instructions
Packages import each other directly or indirectly, creating an illegal circular dependency loop
examples: // package a imports b, package b imports a

patterns.match: non-name .* on left side of dot
patterns.description: Malformed package or selector syntax where a dot selector follows an invalid expression element
Constant expression computation exceeds the maximum bit-width capacity of its target type
Evaluating a constant mathematical division operation where the divisor literal is zero
Bitwise shift operation uses a negative integer constant literal count

patterns.match: type switch guard must be type
patterns.description: Writing a type switch statement syntax without a valid interface value type assertion guard
Switch statement contains multiple case branches checking for the exact same literal or constant value
Type switch guard includes variables or paths without managing concrete matching type cases

patterns.match: can use ... in final argument list only
patterns.description: Using the variadic ... spread operator on an argument that is not positioned as the final parameter

patterns.match: can use ... in array length only
patterns.description: Misusing the ... array size shorthand outside of a fixed array type declaration literal
